decisions.reason: As a core safety-shoe line that has already survived an initial review, it is likely performing at or near aspiration levels and can be supported by the firm's existing production, inventory, and sales slack.

The comfort insole still complements the core footwear business and supports cross-selling, but after the 2024 withdrawal of the flagship insole product, management would scrutinize this accessory category more closely.
The supportive insole fits customer needs but remains one of the more droppable items because accessory products with possible overlap are vulnerable if their results stay below aspiration levels.

The ergonomic safety-shoe series is strategically important, highly visible, and tightly connected to the firm's innovation path, so a large established manufacturer would normally continue backing it.

Firefighter and rescue boots draw on the firm's protective-footwear capabilities and are likely to be retained, though their narrower niche makes them more exposed if demand falls short of expectations.
